title: finding(plugin-detail): RelatedList.lookupLabelResolution renders inside a waitFor predicate — a 50ms lookup-batch delay exhausts the V8 heap and kills the whole vitest worker
body:
Filed by the `os-dev` seat working #7579 (session `session_01KbJQ1y1J12nZxYzFWhP8Q3`), out of a
measurement taken there. #7579 is a one-line value-gate repair; this is a different failure mode
with a different repair, so it is filed rather than folded into that PR.

## What was measured

`RelatedList.lookupLabelResolution.test.tsx` **exhausts the V8 heap and kills its vitest worker**
when the batch lookup-label chain in `RelatedList.tsx` resolves 50ms later than it does today.
Not a slow test and not a failed assertion — the worker dies:

```
Error: Worker exited unexpectedly
...
v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawWithRetryOrFailSlowPath(...)
v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration(...)
Test Files   (1)
     Tests   (2)
    Errors  1 error
  Duration  77.61s (transform 3.30s, setup 204ms, import 6.03s, tests 0ms, ...)
```

`tests 0ms` — nothing was ever reported. `--testTimeout=5000` does not stop it; the allocation
runaway outpaces the timeout. Reproduced on `81a2eb1fb`, four times out of four, in both the
default worker pool and `--pool=forks`.

## The instrument, and the isolation

One timing FACT mutated inside the component and nothing else — the resolution of the
lookup-label batch deferred by 50ms, at the outer `.then` that calls `setLookupLabels`:

```
).then((results) => new Promise((res) => setTimeout(() => res(results), 50))).then((results) => {
```

The mutation was proved on disk before each run (anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, a
`git diff --numstat` naming the file) and restored from HEAD with a blob-hash comparison under a
`trap ... EXIT INT TERM`.

Run file-by-file over the 21 files in `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/` that declare a
`lookup` or `master_detail` field, under that one mutation:

| files | result |
|---|---|
| 20 of 21 | exit 0 |
| `RelatedList.lookupLabelResolution.test.tsx` | exit 1, worker killed |

Package-wide the same mutation kills the run every time (three attempts: default pool,
`--maxWorkers=2`, and the file-by-file loop), so the whole-package census under this probe is
**NOT MEASURED**, not a zero. The narrow two-file run
(`lookupCellLink` + `serverpagination`) is green under the same mutation, so the instrument
itself is sound.

## The reading — stated as a reading, not as the measurement

Both tests in the file poll with a **side-effecting** `waitFor` predicate:

```js
const renderCellText = (value) => {
  const col = h.schema?.columns?.find(...);
  const { container, unmount } = render(FRAGMENT_WITH_col.cell(value));   // mounts into document
  const text = container.textContent;
  unmount();                                                             // and unmounts
  return text;
};
...
await waitFor(() => expect(renderCellText('ps_1')).toBe('排班员权限'));
```

RTL's `waitFor` re-runs its callback on DOM mutations as well as on its interval, and this
callback mutates the DOM on every run. That is self-feeding: the predicate schedules its own next
run. Today the loop terminates almost immediately because the label map lands on the very next
microtask, so the construct is invisible. Give the map 50ms and the loop runs free until the heap
is gone. Testing Library documents the rule this breaks — a `waitFor` callback must be
side-effect free.

That mechanism is consistent with everything measured (heap exhaustion rather than a timeout;
`tests 0ms`; only this file, which is the only one calling `render` inside a `waitFor`), but the
measurement is the OOM, and the causal chain above has not been separately instrumented.

## Why this is worth a card

The failure mode is strictly worse than a flaky assertion for the merge queue. A flaky red fails
one test; a dead worker fails **the whole shard**, and #7075 records that a red here ejects
unrelated PRs — #6959 measured two ejections in fifteen minutes. And 50ms is not an exotic
condition: it is an ordinary CI box under load, which is exactly when a shard is most expensive
to lose.

## What the repair is NOT

⛔ Not #7579's one-line value gate — the assertion here is not reading one resolution too early,
it is the polling itself that allocates. ⛔ Not a widened timeout, which makes the runaway longer.
The direction is to take the side effect out of the predicate: settle the label map with a
side-effect-free `waitFor`, then render the cell once and assert on it. Whoever takes this should
confirm the mechanism above before writing that, since the reading is not yet instrumented, and
should re-run the package census under the same 50ms deferral afterwards — it has never completed.

## Dedupe bound, stated rather than implied

REST `/search/issues` is `403` for this seat (`sessions are bound to their configured
repositories`). The dedupe performed is one targeted MCP `search_issues` over this repo for the
crash shape — `RelatedList lookupLabelResolution test renders inside waitFor callback heap out of
memory worker crash` — which returned `total_count: 0`. A control query in the same shape and the
same session (`RelatedList test settles only the fetch chain then reads a schema-derived value`)
returned 7, including #7075 and #7579, so the zero is a reading rather than a dark channel. That
bound does not cover a card that mentions this file only in its body.

Filed unassigned.

Related: #7579 (the card this came out of), #7075 and #6959.
